proof_summary: For odd \(p\), Fermat’s theorem gives \(2^{p-1}=1\pmod p\); after splitting the shifted sum, every term in its initial block vanishes because its product contains \(2^{2(p-1)}-1\), while the remaining terms match termwise since both the product factors and the triangular exponent are unchanged modulo the period. For \(p=2\), all summands except \(k=0\) vanish and that surviving summand equals \(1\).
